title: Milburn Creek and Bedell's Landing Vicinity
summary: Milburn Creek and the Bedell's Landing area are part of a wider Freeport-Baldwin shoreline landscape where local histories remember Merrick maritime life, shellfishing, wampum-making materials, and stone implements found near the creek.
address_label: Milburn Creek / Baldwin Bay vicinity, Baldwin-Freeport border
ancestral_territory_note: Within and near Merrick ancestral land; connected to the broader creek-and-bay landscape.
why_this_matters: Milburn Creek connects Freeport-area waterways to Merrick shellfishing, wampum-making, travel, and coastal knowledge. The story belongs in a broad creek-and-bay landscape while respecting places that may still hold cultural materials.
introduction_title: A Creek, Bay, and Shellfishing Landscape
introduction_content:
Milburn Creek linked the uplands, marshes, and bay waters along the Freeport-Baldwin border. Local Baldwin histories describe large clam-shell deposits along the creek banks, shell materials used for wampum, and stone implements found over time.

The creek-and-bay landscape carries Merrick maritime history through shellfishing, shoreline travel, wampum economies, and long relationships with the south shore marshes.
history_content:
Nineteenth-century local accounts say that visible shell deposits in the Bedell's Landing area were later removed for fertilizer. The memory of those deposits still points to generations of coastal harvest, travel, and work along the water.

Cow Meadow, Freeport Creek, Baldwin Bay, and Hick's Neck marshes are best understood as connected parts of this south shore cultural landscape.
